plan.title: AD treated vs control Hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The differential expression for the treated (AD lesional) vs control contrast is already delivered as de_results.csv (12,000 genes x 8 columns from DESeq2), so the plan does not refit the model; it starts from those results as the research question requires. Because the raw counts and metadata are also delivered, a Python sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, per-sample library sizes) precedes the enrichment to characterize the structure the delivered DE table inherits — in particular sample_01, whose library size is ~4x below the median; per the low-depth policy it is kept, inspected, and reported, not silently dropped. The DE table is then turned into a full ranked list (every tested gene, ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic — the chosen side of the disputed ranking-metric rule, since it is signed and scaled by its standard error; ties broken by baseMean descending) with gene identifiers resolved into the HGNC symbol space of the pinned gene-set collection, reporting the unmapped share. A preranked GSEA runs that full list against the MSigDB Hallmark human collection (50 sets, 2026.1 release staged locally; 15-500 member size window after intersection with the tested genes, 100,000 permutations, fixed seed, BH adjustment) — the ranked method is used rather than over-representation because the question asks for pathway-level signal across the whole contrast, and a ranked test on the full list retains the coordinated weak signal that thresholding destroys. The report states database + version, rank metric, universe, size window, seed and package versions, lists leading-edge genes per significant set, collapses redundant sets sharing the same leading edge, and presents each set as a method-dependent hypothesis rather than a proven finding. Scope is deliberately limited to the Hallmark collection the question asks for; the staged WikiPathways human GMT is available as a follow-up if requested.

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
